solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Church in Essex’s attacked rampant vices

indicators.note: one thing being in another means it sits inside it
something attacked is knocked about and broken up, so the letters are thrown into a new order

blocks.note: CE is the Church of England
the county name with its possessive S, taken letter by letter

explanation.surface: A church in the county of Essex has been attacked by people with rampant vices.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe-S of Essex's is used as a letter. Essex is an English county east of London.
explanation.definitionFit: Excesses are overindulgences, behaviour beyond moderation, which is what unchecked vices amount to.

clue.text: Old model to tour ancient city for publicity

indicators.note: to tour a place is to go all the way round it, so one piece surrounds another

blocks.note: Ur is the ancient Sumerian city, a crossword favourite

explanation.surface: A former model goes on a tour of an ancient city to get some publicity.
explanation.walkthrough: Model is a verb here, to pose; Ur sits inside it, with EX in front.
explanation.definitionFit: Exposure is being seen and talked about in the media, the same thing as publicity attention.

clue.text: Criminal censorious about knight in the buff

indicators.note: something criminal is wrong or crooked, so the letters are bent into a new order
about means around, so one set of letters goes round another

blocks.note: N is the chess notation for a knight

explanation.surface: A disapproving criminal hangs about a knight who is naked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In the buff' looks like naked, but 'in' is the link and 'the buff' is the definition: a buff is an enthusiast.
explanation.definitionFit: A buff is an expert enthusiast in some field, just as a connoisseur is a discerning expert judge.

clue.text: Drug deal with plebs gone south

indicators.note: a plan that has gone south has gone wrong, so the letters fall into a different order

explanation.surface: A drug deal with some common people has gone badly wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: Plebs are ordinary common folk; here the word is simply letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: A speedball is a narcotic mix of cocaine with heroin, injected or taken together.

clue.text: Heading for emergency, attending nurse is worried

indicators.note: the heading of a word is its top, its opening letter

blocks.note: attending a place is being at it

explanation.surface: A nurse heading to an emergency is anxious about it.
explanation.walkthrough: EN, enrolled nurse, is a standard crossword abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: To be eaten up by something is to be consumed with worry, so eaten works as anxious or troubled.

clue.text: Noise of the enemy passing in ship lingers

indicators.note: being in something means sitting inside its outer letters

blocks.note: time is the enemy, and a clock ticks as time passes

explanation.surface: Sailors hear the enemy fleet go by while the ship stays put.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The enemy' is a crossword name for time, so its passing makes a tick.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that sticks stays around, remaining in place or memory, just as a thing that lingers does.

clue.text: Object if one becomes old pain in the arse?!

indicators.note: one letter becoming another means it is swapped out for its replacement

blocks.note: one is the Roman numeral I
O is the abbreviation for old

explanation.surface: Someone objects if one thing turns into an old nuisance.
explanation.walkthrough: The I in the middle of the object word is replaced by O. 'Object' looks like a verb, to protest, but it is the noun.
explanation.definitionFit: A thong is skimpy underwear worn between the buttocks, literally uncomfortable in the backside, hence the cheeky cryptic hint.

clue.text: Those first in charge of triage for crash site?

indicators.note: the ones first in each word are their opening letters

blocks.note: the opening letters of the three words

explanation.surface: Medics who are in charge of triage at the site of a crash.
explanation.walkthrough: Crash here is slang for going to sleep, not a road accident.
explanation.definitionFit: To crash is informal for falling asleep, and a small bed is a place for doing so.

clue.text: What is carried by asp, rats and fish

indicators.note: what is carried by words is held inside them, running across them

blocks.note: the letters run across the two words

explanation.surface: A question about what diseases snakes and rats spread.
explanation.walkthrough: The asp and rats suggest plague carriers; the letters straddle the comma.
explanation.definitionFit: The sprat is a small silvery sea fish of the herring family, often eaten whole.

clue.text: I bring to order a park officer in hearing

indicators.note: in hearing means as it is heard, so we want the sound rather than the spelling

explanation.surface: A park ranger speaks up at a disciplinary hearing.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition speaks in the first person, as the answer describing itself.
explanation.definitionFit: An arranger puts things in order, or sets music in order for players, so the self-description fits.

clue.text: A French bloke on piano with a sharp smell

indicators.note: in an across clue, one thing on another follows it, so the first-named piece goes second

blocks.note: P is the musical abbreviation for piano
un is the French for a

explanation.surface: A Frenchman sitting at the piano gives off a strong odour.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down-style reading 'on' puts the French bloke after the piano; the piano letter comes first.
explanation.definitionFit: Pungent means having a strong, biting odour or taste, exactly a sharp smell.

clue.text: I crow about head of Opec’s work schedule

indicators.note: the head of a word is its opening letter
about means around, so the larger word goes round the smaller

blocks.note: a roster lists who works when

explanation.surface: Someone boasts about the Opec chief's work timetable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crow' reads as boast, but it is the cockerel's call; the answer speaks of itself.
explanation.definitionFit: A rooster is a male chicken whose dawn call is a crow, so it can say this of itself.

clue.text: A wind soon blows up in a region of Wales

indicators.note: something that blows up is blasted apart and its pieces land in new places

explanation.surface: A gale will soon whip up in a part of Wales.
explanation.walkthrough: Snowdonia is the mountainous area of north-west Wales around Snowdon, its highest peak.
explanation.definitionFit: Snowdonia is a mountainous national park area in the north-west of the country.

clue.text: Good type throwing party provides spirit

blocks.note: G is the abbreviation for good
someone who throws a party hosts it

explanation.surface: A decent sort who throws a party supplies the drink.
explanation.walkthrough: Spirit reads as alcohol at a party, but it means a phantom.
explanation.definitionFit: A ghost is the spirit of a dead person, appearing to the living as an apparition.

clue.text: Men messing with pigeon? It must be beer o’clock!

indicators.note: messing with something leaves it in disarray, so the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: Men fooling about with a pigeon decide it is time for a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It' looks like the start of the exclamation, but it belongs to the letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Opening time is when British pubs open their doors, the jocular hour when drinking may begin.

clue.text: Some fear a stalking dread

indicators.note: some of the words means only part of their run of letters is wanted

blocks.note: the letters run across the three words

explanation.surface: A little fear of being stalked brings dread.
explanation.walkthrough: Dread is not fear here: it is short for dreadlocks, or a person who wears them.
explanation.definitionFit: A dread is informal for a Rastafarian, from the dreadlocks many Rastafarians wear.

clue.text: Father Superior drinks keg when out of head

indicators.note: out of its head means without its top, so the opening letter goes
what drinks something takes it inside

explanation.surface: A Father Superior, head of a monastery, drinks from a keg until he is out of his head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Father Superior' looks like one title, but it splits into definition and wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: To beget is to sire a child, so the one who begets is the parent, the male progenitor.

clue.text: Country pub foremost of bores bothers

indicators.note: the foremost letter of a word is the one at its front

explanation.surface: Tiresome people are a nuisance at the country pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Country pub' reads as a rural inn, but Country is the definition. Bothers is a noun, as in fusses.
explanation.definitionFit: Barbados is an island nation in the eastern Caribbean, independent since 1966.

clue.text: I suppose article on leader’s by The Sun?

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its front letter

blocks.note: the sun rises every morning, so it is a riser

explanation.surface: Someone guesses there is an article about the party leader in The Sun newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: The Sun looks like the British tabloid, but it is the star that rises; the question mark flags the definition by example.
explanation.definitionFit: A theoriser forms ideas and hypotheses, so supposing things is just what such a thinker does.

clue.text: Dieters seen around English diners at midnight?

indicators.note: around means encircling, so one word wraps the other

blocks.note: E is the abbreviation for English

explanation.surface: Slimmers are spotted around English restaurants late at night.
explanation.walkthrough: The midnight feast is a schoolchildren's tradition of secret night-time eating in British boarding-school stories.
explanation.definitionFit: Children at a midnight feast are eating a secret banquet, so they are revellers enjoying a hearty spread.

clue.text: I hate awful old peer consorting with king

indicators.note: something awful is in a terrible state, so the letters are in disorder

blocks.note: R is rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: Someone declares their loathing for a dreadful aged lord who mixes with the king.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition speaks in the first person, as the answer describing itself.
explanation.definitionFit: One who deplores strongly condemns and disapproves, so this person could say they detest things.

clue.text: Film one French article reviewed’s High Society

indicators.note: to review is to look back over something, so the letters run backwards

blocks.note: one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A French newspaper reviews the film High Society.
explanation.walkthrough: High Society is also a 1956 musical film, which makes 'Film' and 'reviewed' look like a review.
explanation.definitionFit: The elite are the top, most privileged group in a society, the upper crust.

clue.text: Bed by dawn (one goes off without issue at last)

indicators.note: a letter going off leaves a gap that another letter fills instead
at last means at the very end, the final letter

blocks.note: a dawn is a beginning, a birth
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: Being in bed by daybreak, with a sly hint that someone has left without having children.
explanation.walkthrough: Dawn as a beginning gives birth; the I leaves and the E stands in its place.
explanation.definitionFit: A berth is a sleeping place on a ship or train, a bunk, so it serves as a bed.

clue.text: Animation originally featured in Top Cat?

indicators.note: originally means at the start, the opening letter
a thing featured in another appears inside it

explanation.surface: Top Cat, the old Hanna-Barbera cartoon, is a starring role in animation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Top Cat' looks like one cartoon name, but it splits: Top is wordplay and Cat? the definition by example.
explanation.definitionFit: A cat is one example of an animal, and beast is a general word for any creature.

clue.text: I thought German should wear stiletto, perhaps

indicators.note: something worn goes on the outside, so it wraps around the wearer

blocks.note: a stiletto is a kind of high heel
G is the abbreviation for German

explanation.surface: Someone muses that a German man ought to wear high heels.
explanation.walkthrough: 'German' looks like the person in the picture, but it is the letter; the answer is himself a German thinker speaking.
explanation.definitionFit: Hegel was a nineteenth-century German philosopher, so his ideas are what he thought, spoken in his own voice.

clue.text: When short dude wears jumpers in plant

indicators.note: something short is cut down, missing its last letter
what is worn goes around the wearer, so one piece wraps another

blocks.note: paras are parachute troops, who jump

explanation.surface: A short man puts on sweaters while working in a factory.
explanation.walkthrough: Jumpers are British sweaters in the surface, but here they are paratroopers.
explanation.definitionFit: Asparagus is a vegetable crop whose young green spears are eaten as a delicacy.

clue.text: One in undersized undies can make you colour

indicators.note: undersized means too small, so the word is cut short
one thing in another sits inside it

blocks.note: pants, British for underpants, cut short
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: Wearing underwear that is too small can make you go red.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain pants means underpants; colour is a verb here.
explanation.definitionFit: To paint something is to apply colour to it, so the verbs are synonyms.

clue.text: Quickly run into a large building company

indicators.note: going into something puts it inside

blocks.note: L is the abbreviation for large
Lego is the toy building-brick company
R is the cricket abbreviation for a run

explanation.surface: Someone dashes quickly into a big construction firm's offices.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Building company' suggests builders, but it is the toy brick maker.
explanation.definitionFit: Allegro is the musical tempo marking meaning brisk and lively, so played fast.

clue.text: Drink Bud after getting up

indicators.note: in a down entry, getting up means rising from the bottom, so the letters read upwards

blocks.note: bud is short for buddy, a pal

explanation.surface: Having a Budweiser beer once you have got out of bed.
explanation.walkthrough: Bud looks like the beer brand but is a friend.
explanation.definitionFit: To lap is to drink with the tongue, as a cat does with milk.

clue.text: All the rage ultimately brews up wrath? Take a breath!

indicators.note: ultimately means in the end, so the final letters are kept

blocks.note: something all the rage is in fashion
the final letter of each word

explanation.surface: Fury is brewing over a fashionable craze, so calm down and breathe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brews up' reads as a phrasal verb, but each word just gives its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Inspire has the old literal sense to breathe in, and the clue is an imperative command.

clue.text: Drink in bed knocked over and spilled on occasion

indicators.note: something knocked over ends up the other way round
on occasion means only now and then, so only every other letter counts

blocks.note: the second, fourth and sixth letters

explanation.surface: A drink in bed gets knocked over and spills now and then.
explanation.walkthrough: Pit is British slang for bed.
explanation.definitionFit: A tipple is an alcoholic drink, especially someone's favourite regular glass.

clue.text: Celeb group back restraining order finally for cranks?

indicators.note: going back means running the letters in the opposite direction
finally points to the end, the last letter
to restrain is to hold in, so one piece holds another

explanation.surface: A celebrity band supports a restraining order against obsessive fans.
explanation.walkthrough: Cranks look like eccentric stalkers, but a crank handle once started a car engine.
explanation.definitionFit: Old cars were started with a crank handle, so cranks are devices that get engines going.
